title.narrative: CERF UFE for Response to Displacement and other priorities in Ethiopia (CERF-ETH-24-UF-1413)

description.narrative: Relief: The government-led returnee process has facilitated the movement of more than 150,000 internally displaced people from the Tigray and Amhara regions to contested Woredas in the southern and northwestern zones. These areas are already experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, affecting many conflict-impacted individuals. Initial assessments by humanitarian partners indicate significant gaps in both food and non-food assistance, raising concerns of worsened humanitarian outcomes if these vulnerable households are not supported in a timely and adequate manner.The WFP and its partners have verified the returnees and provided food assistance during the initial months of their relocation to places of origin. However, significant funding gaps persist, jeopardizing the ability to deliver a predictable response to the food needs of the returnees. Currently, most returnees have limited access to income and food sources.Through other additional funding sources, WFP will provide monthly food rations to other verified returnees and extend assistance to an additional 80,000 severely food-insecure individuals from the local community who are already registered with the WFP. These households will receive pulses purchased with CERF funding, complemented by cereals and vegetable oil from other funding sources. To ensure an effective food response, the WFP will coordinate with partners and local authorities in returnee locations.Logistics Cluster: The Logistics Cluster (LC) facilitates access to common logistics services, sectoral coordination, and information management to address identified logistical challenges. In the Amhara region, where humanitarian actors face mounting difficulties in transporting and storing relief cargo due to deteriorating security and limited infrastructure, the Cluster plays a critical enabling role.With funding from CERF, the LC will significantly scale up its operational capacity to support the wider humanitarian community. This funding will enable the expansion of common services, including temporary storage, coordinated transport solutions, and enhanced information management systems, ensuring the timely and efficient delivery of life-saving assistance to vulnerable populations.The Cluster will increase outreach to over 30 humanitarian partners, particularly in hard-to-reach and high-risk areas of Amhara region, where logistical constraints have severely impacted response efforts. In addition, the Cluster will be better positioned to implement contingency measures that ensure continuity of operations when access disruptions threaten delivery of life-saving critical supplies.As part of its commitment to sustainability and localization, the LC will also capacitate national actors through practical training and skills transfer, strengthening local response capabilities and fostering long-term resilience within the humanitarian logistics ecosystem. As a provider of last resort, the Cluster’s enhanced presence in Amhara ensures that humanitarian partners can overcome logistical bottlenecks and maintain uninterrupted response operations. This expanded support is essential for sustaining humanitarian access and scaling up emergency interventions in one of Ethiopia’s most complex and challenging operational environments. In addition, the Logistics Cluster will provide a broader range of support to humanitarian partners than originally planned, included support in Oromia and Somali regions. This includes:• Leasing of fuel tankers in Amhara, which have been used to refuel trucks carrying Logistics Cluster cargo;• Outsourced manpower for fleet services, including salaries and associated costs for convoy leaders and drivers who have ensured timely movement of humanitarian cargo across the country;• Logistics office costs in Gondar, including security and stock-handling expenses.• The provision of Logistics Cluster support services in Tigray.• Contracting of UNHAS services by the Logistics Cluster.
